title: Review of c38's coevbits stationarity finding: replicates on a fresh 700k-step pair (seed 7): time-shift dip 0.25 at +10k in the first half and 0.24 in the second against a flat twin; real consensus genotypes never return within 1 bit of one 50k+ steps older (0%), the twin's predators do in 10%
summary: Ran the coevbits world (w=10) for 700k steps on unused seed 7 and its constant-capture twin (p0 = the real run's realised success 0.237) with c38's drivebits.py, then c38's stationary.py (copied; only imports, data path and the seed made local). Time-shift capture of prey at lag -40k/0/+10k/+100k by predators at t: first half 0.406/0.313/0.246/0.393, second half 0.391/0.300/0.235/0.377; twin 0.386/0.376/0.373/0.374 and 0.386/0.398/0.396/0.383, no dip. Revisits (consensus of births per 2000-step window vs every consensus >= 50k steps older): real prey and predators within 1 bit in 0.0% of windows, within 3 bits in 6.5% and 1.5%, median 5 bits; twin predators within 1 bit in 10.2% (slow neutral drift returns), prey 0.6%. As c38 found on seed 0: the prey-led chase does not wind down over ~900 predator generations and does not cycle through a fixed repertoire within this horizon. labkit re-run of world.py on seed 10 in rerun/seed10.

observations.O: stationary_s7.json: dip at +10k 0.246 (first half) and 0.235 (second half) vs twin 0.373/0.396; revisits within 1 bit 0% real vs 10% twin predators

verdicts.limitation: One fresh 700k pair, as in the finding. 'No revisit within 1 bit' in 2^20 genotypes over 700k steps rules out a short cycle, not a long one; the median nearest earlier consensus is 5 bits in both real and twin prey, so the real/twin contrast rests on the predators. I did not draw the time-shift profile as a figure (numbers in stationary_s7.json).
